analysis.title: How can I invest in transformational innovation?
key_insights: UBS CIO recommends complementing diversified equity portfolios with targeted exposure to three themes: AI, Power and resources, and Longevity.

UBS estimates overall AI-related capex will reach USD 1.0tr in 2026 and USD 1.4tr in 2027, with agentic AI supporting the next phase. Hyperscalers have raised 2026 capex estimates and project further increases in 2027.
Investors are increasingly focused on AI adoption, monetization, and returns on capital. Elevated expectations and wide differences in company outcomes raise single-stock concentration risk.
UBS favors diversified exposure across the AI value chain: select semiconductors and hardware, mega-cap tech, and more defensive areas of the industry.
AI-linked stocks sold off sharply on 30 October. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 7.2% amid new scrutiny of AI spending going into earnings season.
Data-center demand is accelerating investment in power and grid infrastructure. UBS expects annual sector investment to reach USD 3tr by 2030.

Power and resources opportunities span grid resilience, renewables, nuclear power, industrial automation, and critical minerals. Execution risks and project delays may create volatility, but investment pipelines and order backlogs support the longer-term outlook.
Data centers could account for up to 9% of US electricity use by 2035, versus around 4% currently, based on Bloomberg New Energy Finance forecasts.
UBS is constructive on obesity treatments (GLP-1s) as greater supply and lower pricing broaden patient access. It forecasts 12% average annual revenue growth for global obesity drugs through 2030.
Multiple late-stage trial results in cancer, cardio-metabolic conditions, and neurology in the coming months could be catalysts for Longevity names.
UBS estimates annual global longevity market revenues could reach USD 8tr by 2030, up from USD 5.3tr in 2023.

sector_views.rationale: Strong conviction in long-term AI gains. Favors diversified exposure across select semiconductors, hardware, mega-cap tech and defensive areas, not single-stock concentration.
Data-center demand and electrification drive grid, renewables, nuclear, industrial automation and critical minerals investment, backed by strong order backlogs.
Obesity treatments, late-stage trial catalysts and a growing longevity market support long-term growth.

risk_factors: Single-stock concentration risk in AI given elevated expectations and potentially wide differences in company outcomes.
Execution risks and project delays in power and resources may create volatility.
Scrutiny of AI spending, adoption, monetization and returns on capital.
